requirement: Changing relay/storage/directory/alias must not change AccountID.
Recycled phone numbers must never inherit prior cryptographic identity.
Unknown-sender rejection must be enforceable without trusting sender UI.
Third-party clients must interoperate from public specs/test vectors.
PWA protocol implementation must not create browser-only wire assumptions.
Two clients receiving the same authenticated events in different orders converge semantically.
Attachments are encrypted client-side before provider upload.
No silent downgrade when a bridge/transport exposes plaintext outside OM-native E2EE.
Reference stack runs locally with a small number of boring processes/containers.
Normal users never need to understand keys, relays, federation, object stores, or storage topology.
CryptoProfile migration must normally require no user action and must not change AccountID.
A relay or media provider must not require stable AccountID as a routing identifier.
An active attacker/provider cannot silently negotiate below a previously established security floor.
Changing call path among P2P/TURN/SFU must not change OM-level media confidentiality.
Strict call privacy policy must not expose direct peer IP candidates contrary to policy.
Zero-paid-budget provider policy must prevent avoidable billable usage rather than merely alert after the fact.
Established peers on the same LAN should be able to use direct media and future local messaging/file transfer without cloud media transit.
SMS/MMS/RCS integration must not be required for the first OM-native release or force canonical event redesign.
Report flows disclose only user-selected evidence and cannot require ambient server plaintext access.
Provider failure/migration must preserve identity and canonical conversation meaning.
Discovery provider outage or censorship must not terminate already accepted relationships.
Public discovery records must not expose reusable private relationship delivery capabilities.
A revocable invite can be disabled independently without changing AccountID or existing accepted relationships.
First-contact spam controls are enforceable at IntroGate/relay boundaries without trusting hostile sender clients.
RelaySet entries use distinct opaque capabilities and relay failover does not change canonical EventID or conversation meaning.
Directory lookup can be privacy-split so no single non-colluding provider must learn both client network identity and plaintext alias query.
LAN discovery must not broadcast stable AccountID, username, device name, or other globally linkable OM identifier.
Core OM semantics must remain independent of any particular anti-censorship transport so new transports can be added without identity/history migration.
Default RecoveryPolicy is none; enabling recovery requires explicit user action and does not become a provider master key.
Identity recovery and history-recovery keys/authority are cryptographically separate.
One compromised ordinary control device cannot permanently revoke the healthy control set or manufacture a new control quorum by adding devices.
Quarantine stops future secret distribution to a suspect device without allowing quarantine itself to reduce the constitutional authorization denominator.
Restored/offline devices verify current AccountControlState freshness before exercising control authority.
Personal v1 onboarding can operate with no purchased domain; a workers.dev FQDN may publish signed discovery data.
Share Contact never transfers private pairwise delivery capabilities; forwarded contact data is subject-signed and bounded by expiry/revocation policy.
The basic personal Cloudflare deployment must not require R2/D1/Pages when Worker + SQLite Durable Object can satisfy the zero-payment core.
Official source/release/update trust must not rely solely on one forge, one online signing key, or one mutable CI job.
Recommended/Hardened/Maximum Privacy presets all retain the same minimum approved cryptographic security floor.
Push payloads do not contain normal message plaintext or require the push provider to know canonical conversation identity.
Disabling vendor push communicates platform-specific delivery limitations honestly; iOS silent/background push is not treated as guaranteed.
Backup restore cannot resurrect revoked devices, obsolete recovery policies, obsolete relay capability state, or forbidden CryptoProfiles.
OM v1 does not upload/hash the user's address book by default or as an onboarding requirement.
Local Contacts permission may map/display names entirely on device without transmitting the contact book.
Unknown critical protocol extensions cause the affected operation to fail safely; optional unknown extensions follow explicit ignore/preserve rules.
Nation-state/anonymity transports can be added beneath stable OM semantics without identity/history migration.
Established OM relationships must not require any OM-Project-operated runtime service to continue communication.
The reference PWA and future native clients must share protocol/security semantics through common conformance vectors and preferably one portable OM Core.
No client distribution may receive hidden protocol privileges unavailable to conforming third-party distributions.
PWA Web Push must not require a universal OM push gateway; personal/provider-local push senders remain possible.
Provisioning method is replaceable and must not become identity or protocol state.
Core evidence export is explicit and user-selected; normal operation does not centralize plaintext merely to support hypothetical reports.
A managed/convenience provider can be replaced without changing AccountID or canonical conversation meaning.
Loss of the original project website, primary source forge, author, foundation or business must not terminate established independent OM communication.
Reference source/spec/test vectors should be straightforward to mirror and continue under independent distribution keys.
Official PWA/iOS/Android/Desktop clients use the same security/product semantics through shared om-core and om-ui rather than independent platform rewrites.
Theme bundles must be declarative/non-executable and cannot access message/account/provider data or load arbitrary remote tracking resources.
Themes cannot hide, spoof or semantically alter critical security/control/destructive states or accessibility focus.
Shared UI primitives provide complete keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics, visible focus, text reflow, reduced motion and non-color-only state.
Primary touch controls target at least 44x44 CSS px where practical while retaining compact pointer/keyboard density on desktop.
UI components dispatch typed Core intents and do not directly modify cryptographic, relay, recovery or AccountControlState data.
Core local state should render before network synchronization so startup, conversation open and ordinary local interactions do not block on provider availability.
Reduced-motion preference has a functional mapping for every shared motion primitive; motion must not be required to understand state.
Custom fonts are local/bundled or explicitly permission-selected; themes never silently use third-party font CDNs.
All local/profile-scoped stores, caches, notifications and keys are explicitly IdentityProfile-namespaced; isolation tests cover cross-profile leakage.
PWA origin/provider migration uses authenticated device-link/history-transfer semantics and never treats raw IndexedDB copying as identity continuity.
RichTextV1 and every network/public parser enforce bounded sizes/depth/counts before attacker-controlled allocation/rendering.
No conversation/theme/import path renders arbitrary sender-provided HTML/CSS/JavaScript/WASM.
Every previewable attachment remains untrusted after decryption and passes allowlist/type/size/decompression validation before safe decoding.
Signed/control objects use deterministic canonical bytes with domain separation; non-canonical signed encodings and duplicate-map-key forms are rejected.
AccountControlState CI includes the formal invariants and regression traces defined in FORMAL_VERIFICATION_AND_FUZZING.md.
Default diagnostics never persist plaintext, private/recovery keys, capabilities, bearer tokens or full push subscription endpoints.
Production builds cannot use the dev/test CryptoProvider or experimental profile without an explicit non-production build identity.
Built-in themes provide both light and dark variants; Auto appearance and accessibility overrides work for every theme.
Product engineering must not begin while machine/repository_contract.json has engineering_authorized=false; changing it requires an accepted architecture-freeze ADR.
A conforming OM protocol implementation must be possible from public normative artifacts without a proprietary SDK, secret service, trademark license or SeedLife permission.
Canonical OM must not require a proprietary, royalty-bearing or permission-gated protocol extension/provider as a condition of interoperability.
OM shared Core source uses MPL-2.0 unless a file/component is explicitly assigned another approved license class.
OM reference network-service/provider implementations use AGPL-3.0-or-later unless an ADR establishes a stronger compatibility reason.
Normative protocol schemas, registries, conformance interfaces/vectors and universally reusable protocol-reference artifacts use Apache-2.0.
Architecture/governance/explanatory documentation uses CC-BY-SA-4.0 unless explicitly classified otherwise.
Normal external contributions use DCO 1.1/inbound-equals-outbound and must not require broad copyright assignment or unilateral proprietary-relicensing permission.
Before accepting externally contributed normative protocol mechanisms, OM must have reviewed royalty-free patent-disclosure/license rules sufficient for conforming implementations.
Founder-only S0 project custody must be described honestly; no documentation may claim multi-party project continuity before trustworthy co-stewards actually hold the required roles.
Project/release/domain/store custody must be designed so later trusted maintainers can be added or rotated without migrating user AccountIDs or protocol state.
Asynchronous recipient-device handshake material and MLS KeyPackages are explicit provider-independent protocol objects/capabilities, not hidden central-server assumptions.
Consumable one-time prekeys/KeyPackages must not be mirrored identically across independent providers unless a reviewed construction provides safe shared atomic-consumption semantics.
Key-material depletion or provider failure must never silently downgrade outside the selected CryptoProfile security floor.
One-to-one multi-device messaging has an explicit per-device session-management state machine above the handshake/ratchet and validates device eligibility against AccountControlState.
One user-visible logical message keeps one canonical message identity across per-device session/transport envelopes; fanout must not create duplicate conversation events.
OM groups must define a canonical/conflict procedure for competing MLS Commits from the same epoch before group wire freeze.
Membership/role-affecting OM group-control transitions and corresponding MLS epoch changes must be bound so one cannot silently commit without the other.
RelaySet migration defines authenticated version continuity, bounded overlap and the all-previously-known-routes-unreachable case without globally publishing normal private capabilities.
Attachment/object identity is stable across provider migration; mutable authenticated BlobLocationRecord state provides current locators/repair without rewriting canonical message identity.

Every canonical time/TTL/expiry field declares its clock class, skew/bad-clock behavior and whether it has any authority effect; timestamps alone never authorize AccountControlState/group security transitions.
Self-hosted ClientHost architecture defines signed release discovery, deployment/staging, service-worker lifecycle, rollback/freeze protection, emergency update and compromised-origin migration.
A LinkPreviewProvider must implement SSRF defenses including scheme allowlisting, private/link-local/metadata blocking, DNS/redirect revalidation, rebinding resistance and strict resource bounds.
Provider failure_domain declarations are operational hints, not trusted proof of independent failure domains; security policy may require independently evidenced diversity.
LAN discovery is capability-gated by platform; OM must not require native-equivalent automatic mDNS discovery from all PWA/browser environments.
Every current non-history repository file must have a machine-readable file-registry classification and be covered by manifest validation.
Only one canonical current ProviderCapabilities logical schema may exist outside history at a checkpoint.
Canonical AccountID is cryptographically random 256-bit stable data and must not be derived from a device key, cryptographic algorithm, provider or alias.
AccountControlState is the sole canonical account-authority state object; current normative documents must not define a competing legacy competing authority object.
Every former Q-001..Q-061 record has an explicit resolution/disposition; no generic open-question ledger may silently mix architectural decisions with proof/release/UX work.
Engineering authorization remains false while any architecture_design_queue item is open or any blocks_engineering architecture_verification_gate is not passed.
supersession_note: Global all-gates lock was circular; replaced by scope-granular unlock with two-phase gates (ADR-0108).

requirement: No current canonical legal architecture may privilege one country as OM protocol jurisdiction; project-controlled services/distributions receive role- and jurisdiction-specific review.
Standard project licenses/warranty disclaimers remain intact; a downstream provider/distributor that voluntarily offers warranty, support, commerce, moderation or indemnity does so on its own behalf.
The OM Project must not become a mandatory account, relay, directory, content catalog, bot cloud, marketplace or payment operator solely because the protocol supports those capabilities.
External content-pack provenance/signatures must not be represented as OM Project copyright ownership verification or endorsement.
Any future paid-content feature must keep payment/settlement/merchant operation outside OM Core and must not require an OM-issued token or project-operated payment rail.
Bots/LLMs/bridges that receive plaintext are explicit principals/trust boundaries with scoped authorization and revocation; remote agent context disclosure is never ambient or hidden.
Public/broadcast discovery, if added, is a distinct optional capability/provider surface and must not make private groups globally discoverable by default.
The seven meanings of OM in NAMING.md, including 0M/zero total control, are constitutionally mapped into machine decisions and must not be reduced to a single vendor/product interpretation.
The first usable OM product should provide the ordinary messaging features necessary for traction before prioritizing exotic ecosystem/commerce capabilities.
Private group/Room control and MLS state use the same stable provider-independent ConversationID as ConversationEvents; current architecture must not require a second GroupID alias.
Joining or linking a Space must not silently join/decrypt all child Rooms; every Room retains explicit admission/membership and private-room MLS transitions.
An official Space-to-child affiliation requires authenticated acceptance by both Space and child; unilateral references cannot claim ownership or official membership.

Space-to-Room authority is explicitly delegated and materialized in Room control state; baseline Rooms have at most one authority-parent Space and nested organizational links do not transitively confer authority.

Role management cannot self-escalate: effective authority derives from scoped grants minus explicit restrictions, and any delegated grant must remain within the actor's authenticated grantable ceiling.
Author message deletion and moderator redaction remain distinct authenticated semantics; neither claims remote physical erasure after plaintext delivery.

Public one-to-many Publication events use durable publication authentication suitable for untrusted mirrors; followers are not canonical Publication members and public retraction does not promise erasure.

Private forwarding creates a new destination ConversationEvent and does not carry private source ConversationID/EventID/AccountID/provider transcript by default; scheduled send remains local until normal send unless a future explicit service capability is used.
V1 polls must have deterministic convergent vote/close semantics and must not claim cryptographic voter anonymity unless a separately reviewed anonymous-voting protocol is introduced.

Space/Room/Publication UI must not label link/member/subscriber metadata as cryptographically hidden unless the underlying selective-disclosure design actually provides that property; content E2EE alone is insufficient.
No import/export or migration design may require a SeedLife-operated account/service or intentionally make canonical OM user data hostage to one client/provider format.

Protocol longevity review must define continuity/fork/migration behavior for project/forge/provider disappearance, primitive failure and dominant-client/extension capture before engineering authorization.

Conversation rendering of a sent expressive asset must depend on immutable OM blob/integrity references and bounded fallback metadata, not continued availability of its source pack, catalog, creator site or entitlement service.

Content packs must be inert portable data with immutable releases and provenance/update continuity; pack signatures attest publisher/update control rather than copyright ownership, safety or SeedLife endorsement.

Optional entitlements may gate acquisition or updates but must not become payment settlement, mandatory identity disclosure, DRM, or a rendering dependency for content already intentionally delivered to a recipient.
ConversationEvent authorship must use a typed PrincipalRef plus authenticated endpoint so autonomous services are never represented as synthetic human AccountIDs.

Service installation scope and plaintext/data-access scope must be distinct; selected-context invocation is the default and stable conversation/roster identifiers are withheld unless required/granted.

A full-Room service must be a visible typed plaintext recipient whose cryptographic endpoints are explicitly admitted/revoked; UI-only mentions restrictions must not be presented as cryptographic isolation.
Local model execution, network egress and agent tool calls must be separately capability-authorized; models/plugins receive no raw account, MLS, recovery or governance keys.

Official-client executable plugins must run without ambient filesystem/network/process/environment/secret-store authority; plaintext-read capability must be distinct from network egress and draft capability distinct from send.
Plugin/content publisher signatures provide provenance/update continuity, not trust endorsement; capability expansion on plugin update requires explicit approval rather than inheriting prior grants.

Any extension that changes interoperable shared state must publish protocol semantics/canonical encoding/criticality independent of executable plugin code; opaque proprietary code cannot become mandatory canonical OM semantics.
OM protocol correctness must not require a SeedLife-operated app store, bot store, content-pack catalog, creator marketplace, entitlement issuer or payment service.

Creating a ServiceID and initial ServiceControlState must not require a SeedLife-operated issuer, global bot registry, mandatory catalog, blockchain, domain, phone number or hosting provider; creation itself grants no ambient reach/read/send authority.

OM must not infer a human-versus-AI truth bit: user-confirmed Account actions may remain Account-authored regardless of drafting assistance, while autonomous/delegated actions are ServicePrincipal-authored and any on-behalf-of representation uses a scoped revocable RepresentationGrant.
Service discovery, aliases, catalogs and hosting are replaceable evidence/routing roles; delisting, host failure or alias loss must not replace the underlying ServiceID or transfer its control.

External-network bridges use typed BridgePrincipals; foreign actors/events retain bridge-attested provenance and may not be represented as native AccountPrincipal authors without native OM authorization.

Continuous private-Room bridging/export is explicit authorized trust-boundary state; if the bridge receives plaintext, clients must visibly state that OM-native E2EE terminates at the bridge and external-leg security is separate.

Bridge adapters must expose semantic/fidelity loss and loop/dedup lineage so unsupported edits/deletes/reactions/topics/polls do not silently acquire false OM semantics or reflect indefinitely across networks.

OM defines a public portable archive model independent of any one client/provider; ordinary history archives restore data/evidence but cannot grant Account, Room, Service or Bridge authority or clone DeviceIdentity secrets.

Foreign messenger imports remain provenance-bearing ImportedHistoryRecords or newly shared OM events; importers must never fabricate historical OM EventIDs/AccountPrincipal authorship for foreign data.

The 0M principle requires zero total control: no founder, steward, provider, catalog, dominant client, extension, cloud, app store or government may become an indispensable universal permission boundary for continued OM interoperability.

Normal private relay routing must not require stable AccountID, ConversationID, SpaceID or inner MLS/group identifiers; provider-specific opaque capabilities and encrypted outer transport envelopes are the routing boundary.

OM clients/providers must distinguish protocol-enforced metadata properties from provider-policy claims and must not present content E2EE as proof that IP address, timing, size, membership, push timing or access patterns are hidden.

Per-provider private delivery capabilities and outer ciphertext wrappers must not be intentionally reused across unrelated providers; redundant/failover deliveries use independently randomized transport wrapping where feasible.

Recommended/Hardened/Maximum-Privacy MetadataPolicy may progressively add bounded size padding, private discovery, provider separation, relayed calls, batching or anonymity transports; expensive cover traffic remains explicit and bounded rather than silently mandatory.

Push and blob providers receive only metadata required for their role: vendor push contains no normal plaintext/canonical conversation identity, and blob storage must not require plaintext filenames/MIME/conversation identity; timing/size leakage must remain honestly documented.

OM defines no universal moderator, master blocklist, mandatory safety labeler or global numeric reputation score; abuse enforcement is scoped to the user, relationship, Room, Space, provider or other authority that actually holds the relevant capability/custody.

SafetyAdvisory objects are signed third-party policy inputs whose issuer cannot force subscriber enforcement; non-public principals should use issuer-scoped pseudonymous moderation references where feasible instead of creating a universal cross-labeler identity handle.

Reports disclose selected EvidencePackage material only; private reporter/evidence detail is not automatically embedded in public/shared moderation decisions, and ordinary operation never centralizes plaintext solely to enable future reporting.

Provider moderation/denial/delisting affects only provider custody or reach and cannot mutate AccountID, Room/Space governance, ServiceID/BridgeID ownership or canonical event history outside that authority scope.

Permissionless identity does not imply impossible permanent human-level blocking across Sybil identities; OM must defend unsolicited reach through revocable capabilities, IntroGate/admission policy, scoped rate/resource controls and optional trusted advisories without mandatory global linkability.

Every published protocol generation/profile must be interpretable from mirrorable public artifacts without consulting a live OM Project registry/server; a Protocol Continuity Bundle snapshots normative specs/schemas, registries, conformance vectors, licenses and integrity/release evidence.

Already-assigned protocol/registry identifiers are immutable and never reused for incompatible semantics; incompatible future evolution uses a new profile/registry/fork lineage and fails safely when critical semantics are unknown.

Market dominance does not grant protocol authority: proprietary/permission-gated extensions cannot become mandatory baseline OM conformance, and shared canonical semantics require public independently implementable specifications and conformance behavior.

Crypto/project/distribution failure must never create a universal emergency master key over user identities; use authenticated migration when continuity remains provable and explicit re-verification/successor identity/fork semantics when it does not.

Before public-production resilience is claimed, OM must exercise a creator/forge/domain/provider/release-root disappearance continuity drill using independent mirrors and migration paths while preserving user AccountIDs wherever cryptographic continuity permits.
Onboarding offers at least one path needing no infrastructure-account signup (T0 sponsored starter mailbox or T1 hosted Home); no Home tier or operator is protocol-privileged.

A sponsored starter mailbox is bounded, revocable, non-chainable by default, charged only to the sponsor's own budget policy, discloses its metadata exposure to the sponsor, and can be left for another Home without AccountID change.

Before public-production claims, at least one reference Home implementation with no cloud-vendor-specific dependency passes the same provider conformance suite as the first reference provider; no single vendor may be the only zero-signup onboarding path.

For PWA users, hosting accounts that deploy a ClientHost are endpoint trust: deploy credentials are separate and least-privilege, onboarding steers to phishing-resistant auth where supported, and the client observes release digests against independent transparency sources.

Core computes a local non-authoritative ContinuityAssessment; configurations where one lost device loses identity or locks the constitution show a persistent non-blocking continuity check until recovery, a second controller or explicit acknowledgement.
Every messaging/control device enrollment produces an authenticated, non-suppressible notice on all other active devices of the account; conforming clients cannot complete a device link silently.
OM offers app lock, per-profile lock, quick lock, travel posture and remote suspend, and must not promise hidden-volume/duress deniability without a research ADR and external review.

Clients map each LocalDataClass to platform leakage controls (OS/cloud backup exclusion, file-protection classes, secure surfaces, IME/spellcheck hints, notification cleanup, browser-extension disclosure) and publish a per-platform capability matrix.

Project-controlled distributions publish a security contact and signed advisory channel; profile/protocol-class vulnerabilities use coordinated multi-implementation disclosure; SecurityAdvisories are subscriber-selected inputs, never remote-disable authority.

Security-floor raises are peer-local: a client raises its own minimum CryptoProfile/protocol generation and shows visible 'needs update' relationship states; no distribution can disable another distribution's clients.

AccountRetirement is a terminal constitutional transition authorized by the parent state, RecoveryPolicy or (legacy only) LegacyPolicy; contacts render Closed/Moved and stop sending; providers cannot forge it.

A LegacyPolicy may only retire the account, publish a memorial note and point to a pre-designated successor; it never decrypts history, sends as the account or changes control, and any live controller can cancel it during its contest window.
No UI, profile, documentation or marketing claims post-quantum confidentiality for v1 MLS groups or group calls; PQ status is shown per conversation type from the active CryptoProfile.

The v1 group wire supports an authenticated, downgrade-safe ReInit/migration to a hybrid-PQ MLS profile preserving ConversationID and group authority, adopted automatically once objective triggers are met.
Every verification gate declares pre-engineering criteria, pre-release criteria, independence and unlock scopes; evidence produced solely by the design's author/agent cannot pass a gate.
Engineering unlock is scope-granular; a scope is authorized only by an ADR naming it after every gate listing it and every always-required gate passed pre-engineering criteria.
Every requirement is traced in machine/requirement_traceability.json to at least one verification gate, release gate, validator check, conformance obligation or named review.
Threats are recorded in machine/threat_register.jsonl with validator-checked references to requirements and gates; architecture additions add or update entries.
Later-wave features never block earlier-wave engineering scopes and never add earlier-wave wire requirements beyond frozen V1 extension/criticality points.

Security-critical UX flows (onboarding tier, continuity check, device link notice, suspend device, contact continuity change, bridge E2EE boundary, full-Room service disclosure) pass comprehension testing with non-technical participants before public release.
Operators of public or provider-readable surfaces publish role-scoped illegal-content processes; reference clients perform no client-side scanning of private E2EE plaintext for any authority.
First-contact and discovery surfaces apply current Unicode UTS #39 confusable/mixed-script checks with calm warnings and never convert display names or avatars into verification.

Every new identity is created with identity recovery on (RecoveryPolicy.state=on) using the best available custodian; recovery off is only an explicit, confirmed user choice; a created-without-custodian policy is 'pending' and keeps the continuity check visible.

A recovery request without a co-signing current controller completes only after activation.delay_seconds (>=24h; default 72h Recommended, 7d Hardened/Maximum) with no veto; any live controller can veto; a veto aborts the request and triggers custody rotation; completion revokes all earlier controllers, increments the recovery epoch and notifies contacts; Homes rate-limit recovery requests.
A recovery method contributes exactly one vote toward the floor(N/2)+1 controller majority and may vote immediately only together with at least one current non-quarantined controller.

Recovery custody metadata given to platform credential managers uses a random RecoveryHandle, never the AccountID; identity, provider-metadata, relationship and history recovery use separate domain-separated keys, and only the identity key confers authority.
A T1 hosted Home that evicts a member or closes provides at least 30 days of overlap routes and a guided hand-off to another Home without AccountID change.
A T1 host does not serve its members' ClientHost by default; a same-origin ClientHost is an explicit, labeled member opt-in and the client then treats the host as part of the endpoint trust base.
No W0 scope is authorized while any gate whose interface_impact lists that scope lacks feasibility_status=evidenced.
Reference clients and providers meet the measurable budgets in MOTION_AND_PERFORMANCE.md on reference device classes; a missed budget needs an ADR waiver.

The git repository is the canonical design; design drops are imported only through tools/om_drop.py (base-commit branch + merge + validation), and exported drops carry OM_EXPORT.json and MANIFEST.json and must validate.
Verification CI runs the validator, docs link check, executable evidence and TLC with the digest-pinned tla2tools.jar on every push; regenerated evidence must match committed results.

While project custody is founder-only (S0), the Protocol Continuity Bundle, rebuildable releases and a tested creator-disappearance drill are release requirements, and co-steward recruitment is tracked as a stewardship milestone.

Before public-production resilience claims, the reference T1 host console and the Recommended profile add, by default and where one is reachable, a fallback route on a second provider family for every hosted member; the V-020 vendor-block model shows Cloudflare-first hosting without it leaves about 2% of relationships reachable after a vendor-wide block.

Every IntroGate reserves admission capacity for invite-bound and referral tickets that public (no-invite) requests cannot consume, and the client discloses when public first contact is being rate-limited.
